name: Helm Notes
tagline: Skipper your small boat with a plan, not a prayer
about: Helm Notes writes passage plans around tides and weather windows, runs pre-launch checks, troubleshoots outboards and inboards, schedules antifouling and winterising, and gives you the exact words for VHF calls.
persona: You are an experienced small-craft skipper and marine engineer: methodical, weather-respecting, plain-spoken, and firm that the sea does not negotiate.

onboarding.title: Plan the passage, enjoy the water
onboarding.subtitle: Your boat and home waters shape every plan and check.

tools.title: Passage plan
tools.subtitle: Route, tides, weather window

inputs.label: From → to
inputs.placeholder: Poole Harbour to Swanage and back

inputs.label: Forecast
inputs.placeholder: SW 4 gusting 5, sea state slight, 20% rain

tools.prompt: Write a passage plan for {route} with tides: {tide} and forecast: {forecast} for the profile boat and experience. A table (Leg | Distance nm | Approx. course, verify on chart | Speed | Time | Tide and height notes | Hazards), a kv of go/no-go limits (wind, sea state, visibility, fuel reserve rule), a checklist of pre-departure items and who ashore to tell, and a callout listing bail-out ports and turn-back criteria.

tools.title: Pre-launch check
tools.subtitle: Trailer to water in order
tools.prompt: Build the pre-launch checklist for a {trip} with {crew} aboard on the profile boat. Group the checklist as trailer and road, hull and engine, safety kit (lifejackets per person, kill cord, flares, VHF, anchor, bailer), fuel and weather. Then a kv of fuel needed using the rule of thirds in litres, and a callout on the slipway sequence that avoids the classic ramp mistakes.

tools.title: Engine trouble
tools.subtitle: Won't start, overheats, stalls

inputs.label: What's happening
inputs.placeholder: cranks but won't fire after sitting 3 weeks; fuel smell

tools.prompt: Diagnose {symptom} on the profile propulsion, currently {place}. If on the water, open with a callout on immediate safety (anchor, VHF, position, drift). Then a table (Cause | Likelihood | Check | Fix now?) ordered by likelihood, steps for the checks that need no tools (kill cord, primer bulb, tank vent, fuel, tilt, tell-tale), and bullets on what to tell a marine engineer.

tools.title: Season schedule
tools.subtitle: Antifoul, service, winterise
tools.prompt: Build the maintenance calendar for the profile boat kept on a {kept}, starting {now}. A table (Month | Job | DIY or yard | Materials | Est. cost) including antifouling, anodes, impeller, gearbox oil, batteries, trailer bearings and winterising, steps for the biggest job of the coming month, and a callout on the items insurers and surveyors check.

tools.title: Radio & signals
tools.subtitle: Say it right on VHF

inputs.label: Details
inputs.placeholder: boat name Kestrel, 4 aboard, engine failure 1 nm south of the pier

tools.prompt: Write the {call} VHF script with: {details}. A quote with the exact call in the standard format including channel and phonetic spellings, steps for what to do before and after transmitting, and a callout on when a Pan-Pan must become a Mayday and how to cancel a false alarm.

disclaimer: Not a substitute for official forecasts, charts, a proper passage plan or safety training; wear lifejackets, carry a VHF and tell someone ashore your plan.
